name: Cell–Cell Coupling
description: Paper §Cell–cell coupling (no dedicated figure). Two cell agents are wired to ONE shared environmental nutrient store: each senses the pool and depletes it, so their interfaces are coupled not only through shared state but through CONSTRAINT — one cell's uptake reshapes the other's viability. DRAFT: typed ports + contract, no dynamics. cell_a_proc/cell_b_proc share ONE draft address (local:CellAgent) by design (law 4: one interface, swappable handlers) — the compiler keys handler-env lookup by draft name only (see handler_envs.py note), so per-cell competitive asymmetry (cell_a stronger than cell_b) is carried here, as each node's own `config.vmax`, which the compiler merges on top of the env's shared config.
